I can't tell you how long I spent just trying to decorate my house and upgrade my farm the way I wanted to. The way each character has their own personality, likes, and dislikes, and trying to figure out what they liked, was addicting. I was committed to getting everyone to like me and completing everything for the Community Center to finish the collection.

The yearly events, where you only have one chance each year to collect certain items, made it really satisfying to display them in your house. You can look at each item and remember how you got it.

I got completely lost playing this game, and it felt so relaxing. I can't tell you how many times I said, "Just one more day, then I'll get off," only to find myself playing for another 10 in-game days.

[b]My score: 10/10[/b]
⭐ [b]TL;DR:[/b] The gold standard of cozy and farming games. Unmatched in variety, depth and sheer amount of content, with enough freedom to make the game whatever you want it to be.

🟦 [b]NOTE:[/b] Although I only had around 30 hours on Steam at the time of writing, I've played hundreds of hours on other platforms over the years.

[h2]Overview[/h2]
The best game in its genre, hands down. There's really very little to say: [i]Stardew Valley[/i] is the modern benchmark for cozy and farming games, and I don't think there's anything else on the market that matches its variety, mechanical depth and sheer amount of content.

And, much like [i]No Man's Sky[/i] (read my review [url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/averagemage/recommended/275850/]🔗here[/url]), this is a game that has received constant free updates for ten years, with more still to come. That's an absurd amount of value for a game that already had plenty to offer at launch.

[h2]One Thing I Liked / One Thing I Didn't[/h2]
✔️ [b]Liked:[/b] The sheer flexibility. You can take your time, plan a speedrun to wealth, become a farmer, a rancher, a fisherman, an explorer, or even treat the whole thing like a dating sim. The game rarely tells you how you're supposed to play it.
✖️ [b]Didn't:[/b] The late game can get a little too grindy for my taste.

[h2]Key Points[/h2]
[list]
[*][h3]DIFFICULTY:[/h3] Highly customizable. There is combat and there are time-based challenges, but there are virtually no penalties for ignoring them or coming back when you're better equipped. You can set your own pace and choose how much challenge you want.
[*][h3]PRESENTATION:[/h3] Don't let the almost amateurish-looking sprites and environments fool you: that naïve charm is an integral part of the game's visual identity and remains remarkably consistent. The soundtrack is beautifully composed, with several tracks already considered classics, while the sound effects have been copied by countless other games in the genre.
[*][h3]STORY:[/h3] A classic farming game/cozy game with an ongoing narrative and a touch of magic. The real strength of its story and relationships is that every player gets to experience them differently.
[*][h3]GAMEPLAY:[/h3] You can genuinely do almost anything. If you like fighting, you can fight. If you like fishing, you can fish. If you like exploring, there's plenty to explore. If you like challenges, you have plenty to tackle. If you just want to take it easy, nobody is stopping you.
[*][h3]TECHNICAL POLISH:[/h3] Aside from a few glitches that can occasionally be useful, the game is surprisingly clean and elegant under the hood. Controls and collisions are consistently reliable, and the systems work together with an impressive level of polish, especially considering [b]the game was developed primarily by one person[/b].
[*][h3]MONEYxCONTENT VALUE:[/h3] Absolutely worth it. At €14, it's practically a steal, and there's no real reason to wait for a sale. There's simply too much game here for the price.
[/list]

🟪 [b]NOTE:[/b] If you're into mods, it's worth knowing that ConcernedApe has always been very active in keeping updates compatible with the modding scene. There are countless mods available to refresh or expand the experience, and many of them remain compatible even after major updates. That's a big plus for a developer who clearly understands the needs of PC players.

However, if you're anything like me, a very goal oriented and driven person, this game might fail to be relaxing for you through much of your gameplay.  Because whether its annual events or items that can only be obtained in a certain season, many resources key to progression in this game run on a limited window of availablity.  To add to that, you'll be running around tending to your farm, mining and getting close with the townsfolk.  And if you're hesitant to just say "screw it", throw up your hands and detach yourself from progression, this game can be quite overwhelming.

One of the best places to hang out, decompress, and somehow also be maniacally busy. Concerned Ape (Eric Barone) is a solo-artist, meticulously crafting pixel art, music, items, locations, story, characters, and mystery. His dedication to the community this game has created is inspiring, even ten years later he has announced another major update, adding new content, and as always it will be free to all players on all platforms. 

The game itself is replete with easter eggs, hidden quests, and wonderfully intricate game systems that are well documented in the robust wiki. Almost 500 hours in and I am learning new things about the game all the time. I have solo farms in year 5, co-op farms with so many people, and most recently a four-corners farm with my whole household. What a wonderous space to build together as a family. 

Thank you Eric, 

You should get this game.

The game doesn’t punish you for taking things at your own pace! THE farming game archetype. Used to be Harvest Moon, but now Stardew Valley is the reigning monarch. ConcernedApe is one-of-a-kind developer that still puts out updates years after release, patching bugs, and even has added a couple of huge content patches. In short, this is a labor of love, and it is felt in every part of the game. 

Plus, there's a HUGE modding community, so you kind of get an endless option of variants of the game as soon as you buy it. 

It's hard to find a single game on the store with better value.
This is the best game ever. You should play it. You should try every different farm and play it forever and ever.

This is by far the single greatest game to ever be created. From the gorgeous visuals to the living world to the relaxing and satisfying gameplay look, every single detail is absolutely perfect. Whether you want a cute story game with unique character development, a cozy farming life-sim, or a challenging completionism conquest, Stardew is the perfect game for you. I genuinely cannot recommend this game enough. It's a must play for everyone! Plus, Abigail is my lovely baby girl and I would give anything for her!!
